answer: Client-diversity staking stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer locks a $30 deposit and must serve ten distinct established clients, so one buyer cannot mint ten agents. Second, each client stakes $5 on the job, and escrow pays only on delivery. Third, peers audit one job in six; a failed audit burns the deposit and bans the key 90 days. Fourth, limits grow only after ten distinct clients. Faking 1,000 agents needs 10,000 real client links plus $80,000 at stake, all lost when caught. Like a plume of smoke over real fire, the nectar of trust drifts in on a zephyr of honest work.
